headline: Reviewed park improvement projects at Little City Park, Mansfield Stadium, and Cascade Park, plus summer recreation program results.
summary: The committee heard updates on park projects including tennis court repairs at Little City Park, a new lighting project and field naming at Mansfield Stadium, and ongoing leak repairs at Cascade Park's fountain and pool. Staff also reported strong participation in summer recreation programs such as T-ball, canoe trips, and cheer camp, and noted completion of a historic signage project with University of Maine students. The next meeting is scheduled for October 8th, 2026.
plain_text:
Parks, Recreation & Harbor Advisory Committee 
Council Chambers  
Bangor City Hall 
September 10,2026    5:15pm 
 
Welcome & Introduction: 
Members Present:  Ryan Robbins, Brianna Frye, Michaela Pelkey, Ben Collette,  
          Susan Faloon City Councilor, Pamela Kropp Anderson,  
          Suzette Holly Furrow 
 
Staff Present: Tracy Willette - Parks & Recreation (Director) 
   Chelsie Smith - Parks & Recreation (Recreation Coordinator)  
 
Park Improvements: Tracy Willette  
• Little City Park:  
  The department is addressing cracks in the tennis courts with maintenance  
  repairs this fall, with plans to seek quotes for full resurfacing later. There is also a 
  proposal to replace and relocate the current swing set and potentially add a half- 
  size basketball court in that area  
 
• Mansfield Stadium:  
  The facility held ceremonies to recognize David Mansfield's son, Shawn, and the  
  long-time service of Ron St. Pierre. The field has been officially named  
  Ronald J. St. Pierre  Field at Mansfield Stadium. Additionally, the City is planning  
  a lighting replacement project for the stadium this fall. 
 
• Cascade Park:  
  The park's fountain and pool have been non-operational due to significant, hard- 
  to-locate water leaks. The City's engineering department is currently working on  
  plans and cost estimates to repair the mechanical infrastructure. The fountain  
  and pool at Cascade Park are not working due to significant, hard-to-locate water 
  leaks and mechanical issues within the infrastructure. 
    Key details include: 
• Water loss: The system is losing thousands of gallons of water, with the pool 
losing at least a foot of water during an eight-hour day, making it impossible to 
operate for events. 
• Hidden leaks: The City has struggled to pinpoint the exact location of the leaks. 
Because the plumbing is deep underground, the water does not appear on the 
surface, and the City suspects some drainage may be occurring into the 
stormwater system. 
• Mechanical failure: The pump pit is also experiencing constant water infiltration, 
creating additional challenges for maintenance. 
• Status: The City is currently working with the Engineering Department to develop 
a plan and get cost estimates for a comprehensive repair of the pool, plumbing, 
and fountain, with the goal of preserving the historic park's infrastructure for the 
long term.
• Community Garden:  
 The City has approved funding to renovate the parking area at the community 
 garden to create a more organized space and potentially allow for future garden 
 expansion. 
 
Recreational Program Update: Chelsie Smith 
• T-ball: Experienced a massive increase, growing from only 7 registered participants in 
 2025 to 71 kids this year. 
• Youth-Guided Canoe Trips: Participation doubled compared to the previous year, with 
 13 participants in the sessions led by Maine Guide Jim Fahey. 
• Culinary Camp: Proved to be extremely popular, filling up all available spots within just 
 two days. 
• Summer Cheer Camp: A new program introduced this year that was highly successful, 
 reaching its maximum capacity of 46 participants. 
• Adult Kickball: A newly launched low-impact sport that successfully registered eight 
 teams in its first year, despite a tight 45-day lead time for setup. 
• Youth Football Clinic: Through a partnership with Bangor High School coaches and 
 athletes, 44 children in grades 3-5 were enrolled for free. 
 
Other Business: Tracy Willette 
• Historic Signage: A project involving University of Maine students to install and update 
nine historical interpretive signs throughout the city has been completed. 
• Future Planning: The committee discussed the potential for future Recreation Center 
proposals 
• Next meeting for the October 8th, 2026 
 
Adjourned at 6:25pm
